canSpam.title: CAN-SPAM basics (United States)
canSpam.appliesTo: Commercial email: any email that advertises or promotes what you sell, including emails to people who signed up.

rules.detail: Your From name, From address and Reply-To must show who you are.
The subject line must match what is in the email. No fake RE: or FWD:.
A promotional email has to be identifiable as an ad. You have leeway in how you say it.
Every email carries a valid postal address: a street address, a USPS post office box, or a private mailbox registered with a mail receiving agency.

rules.rule: A clear way to opt out
rules.detail: Every email explains how to stop getting your emails. An unsubscribe link in the footer does it.
Stop emailing people within 10 business days of an opt-out. The opt-out has to keep working for at least 30 days after you send, can't cost money and can't ask for more than an email address.
If someone sends email for you, you are still responsible for following the law.

canSpam.penalty: Each email that breaks the law can cost up to $53,088 under the FTC's January 2025 adjustment. The amount is adjusted every year, so check the FTC page for today's number.

gmail.title: Gmail's sender rules
allSenders: Set up SPF or DKIM for the domain you send from. Your email tool shows the records to add.
Keep spam reports under 0.3% (Google suggests aiming for under 0.1%).

bulkSenders.threshold: 5,000 or more emails a day to Gmail addresses
rules: SPF, DKIM and DMARC all set up
One-click unsubscribe in marketing emails, plus a visible unsubscribe link in the email
